Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 8 th Of October, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 9797 of 2024
 Nargis Bee And Others
 Versus
 Gyan Singh And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Rohan Malviya, Advocate appearing on behalf of Shr  Malviya, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Manoj Kumar Soni, learned counsel for the responde  ORDER
The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 01.08.2024 passed in MACC No.1152/2022 challenging quantum of compensation.
2. The short facts of case are that 20/02/2022, Shahid Ansari along with his father was coming to Ujjain from Indore on his motorcycle.

When he reached near Hotel Rudraksh near Shani 'Temple,
the driver of a car bearing registration number MP13-CA-9116 came driving the same in rash and negligent manner and rammed into the motorcycle of Shahid due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was rushed to hospital, however, he died during the treatment.
3. The appellants/claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Shahid.

It was claimed in the claim petition that at the time of accident he was earning Rs.16000/- per month by doing private work as supervisor at Swarana Saw Mills, Agar Maksi Link Road, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:30413 2 MA-9797-2024 Ujjain.
The claims tribunal after considering the evidence available on record concluded that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the insured vehicle.
Thus, the insurance company was saddled with the liability to pay compensation which was quantified at Rs.21,16,082/-.

4. The learned counsel for the appellants submits that the income of the deceased Shahid has been taken at Rs.8800/- per month on notional basis by taking him an unskilled labourer, however, the deceased was working as supervisor.
Thus, he cannot be treated as unskilled labourer.

His income should be taken as Rs.16000/- per month which was duly proved by statement of Nargis Ansari Nargis Bee vs Gyan Singh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158907793/
1 AW-1.

sentences.text:
He also submits that looking to the peculiar facts of the present case inasmuch as the the appellant No.1/the widow of the deceased and appellant Nos.2 and 3 are minor children, who were around 6 months, 7 years and 12 years of age respectively at the time of accident and old parents,
the deduction should have been taken at 1/5th.

He also submits that the claims tribunal has incorrectly disallowed the entire reimbursement of the expenditure incurred in treatment of the deceased at Rs.2,50,000/- and the claims tribunal has awarded the amount of Rs.1,55,882/-, thus,
he prays for enhancement of compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company points out by referring the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 13 of the award.
He points out that there was no material at all to prove that the deceased was working as supervisor and earning Rs.16,000/- per month.
He thus submits that looking to number of claimants at 6, the claims tribunal has correctly made deduction as 1/4th.

He further submits that Ex.P-19 to Ex.P-38 were the bills which were produced by the claimants according to which expenses in treatment of the deceased have been awarded by the claims tribunal, thus, no interference is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:30413 3 MA-9797-2024 warranted in the matter.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

From the evidence available on record as well as statement of AW-1 Nargis Ansari, it is seen that claim was made that the deceased was working as supervisor, however, there is no material at all to show that he was employed on the said post and was being paid salary of Rs.16000/- per month.
No evidence at all has been brought on record for demonstrating the same.

8. As regards the income, the claims tribunal has taken the income of the deceased on notional basis at Rs.8800/- per month which was the prescribed minimum wages for an unskilled labourer at the relevant time.
In the considered view of this Court, no interference is warranted in the same also.

However, it is seen from the record that claims tribunal has not awarded entire amount of medical expenditure, hence, it is hereby directed that a further amount of Rs.50,000/- shall be paid to the appellants over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of the application before the claims tribunal.
Rest of the findings of the tribunal shall remain intact.
9. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
